$description:
Surface contract — the STATIC, in-flow container/panel (cards, panels,
frames, sections, accordion containers, windows). The counterpart to OVERLAY:
same "grouped surface" idea, but no z-stacking / elevation-above-page — it
sits IN the flow.

Lean by design (see the taxonomy spec): semantics carry the default look — the
recipe reads --a63-surface-panel (bg), --a63-border-subtle (border),
--radius-* (radius), --a63-text-* (text) at the use-site. The ONE thing themes
vary distinctly for a static surface is its FLUSH-vs-LIFT-vs-BEVEL treatment,
so that is the only contract token here.

--a63-surface-shadow is a drop/bevel (mode-independent), so it's safe to
default at :root and let each theme override it on its shell (modern soft-flush,
aqua subtle glassy lift, retro hard Win98 frame bevel, terminal phosphor edge).

The contract now carries the full treatment vocabulary
(gloss/highlight/backdrop/border/texture/inner-shadow), not just the shadow.

Radius is intentionally NOT defaulted here — recipes read
   var(--a63-surface-radius, <own default>); a theme sets it to square all
   surfaces (retro → 0). Declaring it here would flatten per-recipe radii, so
   it stays unset at :root.

$extensions.io.atom63.derive: 0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklch, black 6%, transparent), 0 1px 1px color-mix(in oklch, black 4%, transparent)

shadow.$description: Outer elevation — flush · bevel · drop · glow (existing lever, unchanged).

Recessed/inset treatment (sunken well). `0 0 #0000` = flat.
   NOT `none`: this token is composed into comma-separated box-shadow lists
   (`var(--a63-surface-inner-shadow), var(--a63-surface-shadow)`), and `none`
   is only legal as the sole value — it invalidates the whole declaration and
   silently drops the surface's elevation.
